# What's new at Envoy: October 2026 product releases

Nov 2, 2026

Manage emergency notifications and emergency response teams across every location with Envoy Response, and learn how customers are using threat intelligence and incident management.

### Stay in the know

Get the latest from Envoy sent straight to your inbox.

An emergency rarely stays inside one building. A storm warning, a protest, or criminal activity nearby can affect several sites at once. The people responsible for safety have to answer three questions fast: _what is affected, who is there, and have they been told?_

Employees feel the gap. In [Envoy's July 2026 survey](https://envoy.com/workplace-compliance-security-safety/workplace-safety-report-2026) of 1,000 U.S. workers, 74% said they have avoided going to work because of a threat, and only 40% said they hear about disruptions from official employer or HR communication.

[Envoy Response](https://envoy.com/products/critical-event-management) is built for these moments, and these October 2026 product updates improve how you scale emergency readiness across your footprint.

## **Global settings, local preparedness**

Global admins can standardize Response settings for every location from the Global overview, while location admins keep control of their own sites.

- **Set location-specific emergency notification settings from the Global overview:** Select locations one at a time, by location group or all at once. This closes gaps before an incident: a location needs emergency notifications turned on before its admins can use two-way chat, safe and need-help responses, and roll call, and employees need a phone number in their profile to receive SMS alerts.

[Learn more about global settings for emergency notifications](https://envoy.help/en/articles/17300819-global-response-settings) →

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6509fe179d7033a278a05268/6ae50ab8c63400fde524a109_b8ba655e.png)

Manage location settings globally.

- **Manage employee phone number collection:** Employees need a phone number in their Envoy profile to receive SMS emergency notifications. Admins can prompt employees to add a phone number, for many locations at once from Global overview. When this setting is on, employees without a phone number see a banner on the dashboard and the mobile app homepage prompting them to add one. Each setting shows how many locations it is on for, so you can see where coverage is missing.

[Learn more about how to prompt employees to enter their phone numbers](https://envoy.help/en/articles/17300819-global-response-settings?utm_source=chatgpt.com#h_3ae441440b) →

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6509fe179d7033a278a05268/6ae5062e21cbca5b754e591e_phone-number-banner.png)

Prompt employees to enter their phone numbers.

- **Assign local emergency response team members to multiple locations:**

Admins can set emergency response team (ERT) members by location, all from the centralized Global overview. That way the right people are kept informed and emergency  response stays local: two-way replies and requests for help go to the people closest to the incident, not to every admin in the organization.

[Learn more about setting emergency response teams](https://envoy.help/en/articles/17300819-global-response-settings#h_3ae441440b) →

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6509fe179d7033a278a05268/6ae50ab8c63400fde524a10c_d77b76cd.png)

Assign local emergency response teams.

Building your ERT teams follows the same approach as our guide to [emergency response roles at work](https://envoy.com/workplace-compliance-security-safety/emergency-response-roles): keep the core roles consistent, assign coverage by location or shift, and make sure local teams know what they own and when to escalate to a central response team.

- **Timestamps on emergency notifications:** Recipients can clearly see when an emergency notification was sent so that directions are up to date.This UI update applies across all channels through which emergency notifications can be sent: SMS, Slack, push, email, and Teams.

![Smartphone screen displaying an active fire evacuation alert from Envoy app at San Francisco HQ, instructing immediate evacuation via stairs to the muster point and requesting user response with options 'I'm safe' or 'I need help'. Alert sent by Maya Johnson, Head of Workplace, at 11:22 AM PDT.](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6509fe179d7033a278a05268/6ae91a289e27eed3077764ec_fire-evacuation-web-alert-dark.png)

Timestamps in emergency notification.

## **Real-world readiness: How one security team used Envoy Response**

About 40 minutes before Target Field opened for a Minnesota Twins game this past September, someone opened fire nine blocks away in downtown Minneapolis. Read the [Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com/91622633/how-the-minnesota-twins-kept-fans-safe-during-a-recent-nearby-shooting) article about how the Director of Security used Envoy Response to alert roughly 500 employees and 78 others who might be nearby, and sent an all-clear 25 minutes later.
